Well-established. || Phase 3 trials and multiple meta-analyses confirm HbA1c reduction (~-0.5 to -0.6% monotherapy WMD; -0.53% as combo). FDA approved; first generic approved 2026-04-07.

dapagliflozin -> inflammation.evidence_summary: Multiple RCTs and mechanistic studies confirm dapagliflozin reduces NLRP3 inflammasome activation, lowers IL-1β/IL-6/TNF-α. Nature Comms 2020 (PMID 32332732) shows SGLT2i modulates NLRP3 via ketones. Springer 2017 shows dapagliflozin reduces NLRP3/ASC/caspase-1 in diabetic cardiomyopathy mice.
dapagliflozin -> inflammation.validation_notes: 2026-06-20 web re-validation: 18-RCT meta-analysis (5,311 pts) shows SGLT2i significantly lower IL-6, with dapagliflozin the highest-potency agent vs empa/cana. Clinical RCT (Cardiovascular Diabetology 2024) confirms dapagliflozin reduces systemic inflammation in T2D without HF. NLRP3/itaconate + ketone mechanism corroborated. Top-level status reconciled PARTIALLY_VALIDATED->VALIDATED to match internal validation_status (was stale since 2026-03-20).

verapamil -> T1D.validation_notes: April 2026 re-validation: (1) 2018 Ovalle RCT (PMID 29988125) positive for C-peptide AUC preservation at 3/12mo; (2) 2023 Forlenza pediatric RCT positive for C-peptide preservation; (3) 2023 meta-analysis (PMC10424102) across adult+ped RCTs (112 pts) showed significant 1-yr C-peptide benefit; (4) 2025 Ver-A-T1D European multicentre RCT (n=136) — primary endpoint (2h MMTT C-peptide AUC at 12mo) MISSED statistical significance; trend favored verapamil; results presented EASD Sep 2025; Ver-A-Long OL extension ongoing to 24-36mo; (5) 2026 systematic review PMID 40111679 (Cardiovascular Drugs and Therapy) concluded verapamil is safe adjunct with glycemic-control signal but flagged limited scale/heterogeneity. Net interpretation: benefit signal is real but effect size is modest and heterogeneous across trials; the largest/most-recent RCT did NOT confirm primary endpoint. Confidence DOWNGRADED from HIGH to MEDIUM. Do not over-state beta-cell preservation claim. || REFRESH 2026-07-10: Re-checked for Ver-A-T1D 24mo / Ver-A-Long extension readout - NONE yet published (trial continues to 24mo then 3-yr OL extension; Pieber group planning RCT meta-analysis + larger/longer repeat). Net evidence picture now slightly more cautious: smallest/earliest RCTs (Ovalle 2018 PMID 29988125; Forlenza pediatric 2023) + 112-pt 2023 meta-analysis positive for 1-yr C-peptide, but the largest, most rigorous adult RCT Ver-A-T1D (n=136, 21 sites) MISSED primary 2h-MMTT C-peptide AUC at 3/6/9/12mo (EASD Sep 2025), only non-sig favorable trend. Status held PARTIALLY_VALIDATED; direction=mixed leaning cautious pending extension + planned meta-analysis.

verapamil -> beta_cell.evidence_summary: Mixed evidence: 2018 Ovalle/Shalev Nat Med RCT positive (PMID 29988125); 2023 Forlenza pediatric RCT positive; 2023 meta-analysis of RCTs (PMC10424102) positive for 1-yr C-peptide benefit. 2025 Ver-A-T1D (European multicentre RCT, n=136, results at EASD 2025) — primary MMTT C-peptide AUC endpoint did NOT reach significance at 3/6/9/12mo (numerical trend favored verapamil). 2026 systematic review PMID 40111679 confirms safety and a glycemic-control signal but cautions about scale/heterogeneity. Preclinical mechanism (TXNIP suppression, β-cell mitochondrial respiration) remains intact. Confidence MEDIUM: evidence of biological signal but an adequately powered contemporary multicentre RCT did not confirm the primary endpoint.
verapamil -> beta_cell.validation_notes: 2026-06-13 web re-validation: CLVer pediatric RCT (PMID 36826844, JAMA 2023) showed verapamil preserved stimulated C-peptide ~30% above placebo at 52wk; Ovalle adult RCT (PMID 29988125, Nat Med 2018) positive for C-peptide AUC preservation. Ver-A-T1D European multicentre adult RCT (n=136, 21 sites/6 countries; protocol/design PMID 39613428, BMJ Open 2024) underway -- final peer-reviewed primary results still pending (tracked in queue, next ~2026-07-02). Mechanism (Ca-channel blockade -> reduced TXNIP -> beta-cell survival) established. Upgraded PARTIALLY_VALIDATED->VALIDATED on strength of two positive RCTs + supportive meta-analysis; effect is PARTIAL preservation, durability beyond 12mo not yet established.

NF_kB -> inflammation.evidence_summary: NF-κB is a well-established master regulator of inflammatory responses in diabetes. Multiple reviews confirm: Frontiers Pharmacology 2017 (PMC5681994), Cell Metab 2011 (PMC3040418). Salicylate/IKKβ inhibition improves glucose tolerance in T2D patients. Curcumin modulates NF-κB to reduce oxidative stress in diabetes (Zamanian 2024).

empagliflozin -> inflammation.evidence_summary: EMPA-CARD RCT showed empagliflozin reduced IL-6 (-1.06 pg/mL, p=0.006) and hs-CRP (-2.86 mg/L, p=0.003) vs placebo. 12-month trial showed 54% hs-CRP reduction. Meta-analysis confirms CRP reduction -0.63 mg/L (p=0.01) and IL-6 SMD -0.28 (p=0.03). EMPA-REG OUTCOME supports cardiovascular benefits partly via anti-inflammatory effects. [2026-07-05 refresh] SGLT2i IL-6 meta-analysis (PMC10668472, 18 RCTs, n=5,311) confirms class-level IL-6 reduction, BUT reports dapagliflozin > empagliflozin for IL-6 lowering, and EMPIRE-HF showed NO hs-CRP effect in heart-failure patients - anti-inflammatory signal is population-dependent (strongest in T2D+CAD, e.g. EMPA-CARD). Empagliflozin+colchicine post-STEMI SR (PMC12536377) relevant to the hub's SGLT2i+anti-inflammatory combination theme. Core signal holds but heterogeneous across populations -> retain PARTIALLY_VALIDATED (not full).

dapagliflozin -> nephropathy.validation_notes: DAPA-CKD landmark RCT (NEJM 2020 PMID 32970396, n=4304): dapagliflozin 10 mg vs placebo over median 2.4 y reduced composite (sustained ≥50% eGFR decline, ESKD, renal or CV death) HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.51-0.72). Confirmed by 2024 SR/MA (PMC11370938, 9 RCTs, ~30k participants) showing OR 0.61 (0.57-0.65) for primary kidney composite and OR 0.69 (0.63-0.76) for mortality, with UACR reduction of -23.99% (95% CI -34.82 to -13.15). Effect present in patients with and without T2D. Mechanism strongly supported.

pioglitazone -> T2D.validation_notes: PROactive RCT n=5238 (PMC2291341): 16% reduction in composite MACE; insulin progression halved. Meta-analyses (Nat Sci Rep 2019, PLOS One PMC2701605) confirm glycemic efficacy with weight gain & edema caveats. Caveat: pioglitazone HbA1c effect as monotherapy is comparable to comparators (not superior) but FPG improved.

external_refs: PMID 41357229 / PMC12675237 (2025 review): Targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome in kidney disease - molecular mechanisms, pathogenic roles, and emerging small-molecule therapeutics. Catalogs DKD-relevant candidates (selnoflast, dapansutrile, DFV890, NT0796, ZYIL1, MCC950).
PMC9218738: NLRP3 inflammasome mediates glomerular and tubular injury in diabetic nephropathy (mechanistic).
Molecular Therapy S1525-0016(24)00745-7: CRP promotes DKD via Smad3-mediated NLRP3 activation.
MDPI IJMS 27(10):4257 (2026): NLRP3 inhibition attenuates diabetic kidney injury via suppression of ferroptosis (in vivo/in vitro).
COUNTER-SIGNAL PMC8777085: MCC950 produced ADVERSE renal effects in one interventional DKD model - mechanism is context-dependent.
validation_evidence.rationale: Mechanistic support for NLRP3 in DKD is strong and consistent across multiple 2024-2026 models, and several NLRP3 inhibitors are in clinical development. But NO NLRP3-inhibitor RCT has yet reported a renal primary endpoint in DKD, and at least one preclinical model (MCC950) showed adverse renal effects. Mechanism validated; clinical efficacy unproven -> PARTIALLY_VALIDATED.

audit_history.finding: Single-source dependency confirmed: corpus support is PMID 39412512 alone (J Bras Nefrol 2024), a NARRATIVE REVIEW, not a systematic review or meta-analysis. It is also MISSING from paper_library/index.json despite contributing 61 data points to NLRP3_inflammasome -> inflammation. PMID verified live via NCBI esummary - real, correctly titled, not fabricated. Rating retained but the mechanistic/preclinical ceiling is reaffirmed: still no NLRP3-inhibitor RCT with renal endpoints in DKD.
audit_history.action: Queued index backfill for 39412512; data_point_count for NLRP3->inflammation should be treated as review-derived, not primary-study-derived.

dorzagliatin -> T2D.validation_notes: SEED phase 3 (PMID 35551294, Nat Med 2022): drug-naive T2D n=463, HbA1c -1.07% vs -0.50% placebo at 24wk. DAWN phase 3 (PMC9117147): add-on to metformin n=767, HbA1c -1.02% vs -0.36%. Both no severe hypoglycemia/drug-related SAEs.

rapamycin -> inflammation.validation_notes: 2026-06-21 re-validation: effect remains PRECLINICAL and context-dependent. Rapamycin reverses inflammatory-cytokine-induced IRS-1 serine phosphorylation and restores IRS1/PI3K/AKT insulin signaling in vitro/in vivo (PMC4598825); single-dose attenuates post-ischemic cardiac fibrosis+inflammation in diabetic model (PMC10218967). BUT mTOR inhibition is paradoxical - induces hyperglycemia/new-onset diabetes in 13-50% of oncology trials (PMID 26421362). No human anti-inflammatory RCT in a diabetes population. Rating unchanged.

hydroxychloroquine -> inflammation.evidence_summary: Systematic review & meta-analysis (PMC9196294 / PMID 35687592) and >=3 RCTs in T2D show HCQ improves glycemic control (HbA1c reduction) and lowers CRP/TNF-alpha/IL-1/IL-6; approved as an oral antidiabetic in India. RCT in insulin-resistant adults (PMID 33528893) tested insulin sensitivity/inflammation. Anti-inflammatory effect is RCT-supported but usually a secondary endpoint; large long-term safety RCTs still pending -> MODERATE confidence.
hydroxychloroquine -> inflammation.validation_notes: 2026-06-20 web validation: upgraded PARTIALLY_VALIDATED->VALIDATED on strength of SR/MA + multiple RCTs; retinal/cardiac safety monitoring caveat noted.

semaglutide -> retinopathy.validation_notes: 2026-06-20 web re-validation: 2025 SR/MA (78 RCTs, 73,640 pts, searched to Apr 2025) found NO net effect on diabetic retinopathy (OR 1.04, 95% CI 0.92-1.17) BUT a raised NAION signal (OR 3.92, 95% CI 1.02-15.02). SUSTAIN-6 early-worsening signal in pre-existing DR persists mechanistically (rapid glucose-lowering). Dedicated FOCUS RCT (1,500 T2D pts) ongoing, completes 2027. Remains PARTIALLY_VALIDATED: mechanistic early-worsening concern real, net DR risk not confirmed; await FOCUS. | 2026-07-06 reaffirm PARTIALLY_VALIDATED: early transient retinopathy-worsening signal tied to rapid glycemic improvement (SUSTAIN-6); long-term effect inconsistent/inconclusive, tends to stabilize after 12-18mo. 2025 systematic review of GLP-1RA microvascular outcomes (PMC12547187) corroborates mixed retinopathy evidence. Definitive FOCUS RCT (n=1500) results now expected 2026 (completion 2027) - added as monitoring watch. Status unchanged.

metformin -> nephropathy.validation_notes: 2024 J Clin Endocrinol Metab (PMID 38986038) and 2015 Annals Int Med systematic review (PMID 25536258) show metformin associated with lower incidence of doubling serum creatinine, eGFR ≤15, and ESKD in T2D. Combination with SGLT2i further reduces composite kidney outcomes. NOTE: PARTIALLY_VALIDATED because effect derives largely from observational and cohort data; no dedicated RCT for nephropathy as primary endpoint (vs. SGLT2i which have CKD-primary RCTs). Cross-validated 2026-05-12. | RE-AUDIT 2026-06-28: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. New 2026 SR/MA (Eur J Pharmacol, ScienceDirect S0014299926000427, search to Sep 2025) on metformin safety in CKD+T2D (all-cause mortality, MACE, ESRD, lactic acidosis) and a nationwide Scottish target-trial-emulation (stopping vs continuing metformin in advanced CKD) support a renal-protective/safety signal, BUT still NO RCT with nephropathy/CKD as primary endpoint (contrast SGLT2i). Tier unchanged. | MON-SWEEP 2026-08-10: The 2026 Eur J Pharmacol SR/MA previously cited by DOI (ScienceDirect S0014299926000427) now resolves to real PMID 41548682 (12 studies, search to Sep-2025): all-cause mortality HR 0.76 (0.64-0.90), ESRD HR 0.61 (0.49-0.76), lactic-acidosis trend in stage-4 CKD HR 1.93 (0.95-3.87), no MACE association; certainty VERY LOW (observational). Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED: renal-protective/safety signal strengthens but still NO RCT with nephropathy/CKD as primary endpoint (contrast SGLT2i CKD-primary RCTs).

vitamin_d -> autoimmune.validation_notes: PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. Observational meta-analysis (Zipitis & Akobeng 2008; Dong 2013 Nutrients PMID 24036529) suggests early-life vitamin D supplementation reduces T1D risk (OR ~0.71). ABIS study (PMID 17341286) found no protective effect on islet autoimmunity in unselected infants. 2025 Frontiers immunology meta-analysis indicates modest reductions in autoimmunity with supplementation in at-risk children. No prevention RCT has shown definitive T1D incidence reduction. Mechanistic plausibility (VDR on immune cells, regulatory T-cell modulation) is solid. Cross-validated 2026-05-12.

metformin -> cardiovascular.validation_notes: UKPDS 34 (Lancet 1998, PMID 9742976): metformin in overweight T2D reduced all-cause mortality 36% and diabetes-related death 42%. Griffin 2017 Diabetologia meta-analysis (PMID 28770324, 13 RCTs n~4,158): all CV effect sizes favor metformin but none statistically significant (all-cause RR 0.96, MI RR 0.89, CV death RR 0.97). Boussageon 2012 PLoS Med (PMID 22473097) similarly equivocal. PARTIALLY_VALIDATED: foundational UKPDS evidence + biological plausibility, but updated RCT-level meta-analyses do not show consistent significant CV benefit; observational data favorable. Cross-validated 2026-05-12.

tacrolimus -> inflammation.notes: Tacrolimus inhibits NF-kB / NFAT in T cells (PMID 23573283 PLOS One) suppressing TNFa/IL-6/IL-1 -- canonical anti-inflammatory effect. BUT cell-type dependent: PMID 27291296 (Sci Rep) shows TAC induces vascular inflammation via TLR4. PMID 23958496 shows TAC activates NF-kB in tubular cells via JAK2/JNK/TLR4. Net effect: anti-inflammatory in T cells, pro-inflammatory in vascular/renal tissue. Cannot be summarized as simple anti-inflammatory. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified: 23573283 (Maguire 2013 PLOS One: TAC inhibits NF-kB in T cells), 23958496 (Gonzalez-Guerrero 2013: CNIs activate NF-kB in tubular cells via JAK2/JNK/TLR4). Effect is cell-type dependent.

calcineurin -> islet_transplant.notes: Calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus, cyclosporine) are diabetogenic and beta-cell toxic. PMID 25255841 (Drug Metab Toxicol 2014) review: CNIs reduce insulin secretion, transcription, induce apoptosis; impair Ca++ flux. PMID 17176613: CNI substitution with MMF resolved beta-cell toxicity in islet recipient. PMID 37359825 (Posselt 2023, Transpl Int): calcineurin-SPARING regimen maintains long-term insulin independence. Validated direction: CNIs HARM islet grafts; field is moving to calcineurin-sparing protocols. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified: 17176613 (CNI substitution resolves beta-cell tox), 25255841 (Tacrolimus pancreas Tx review), 37359825 (Posselt 2023 calcineurin-sparing).

metformin -> inflammation.notes: Metformin anti-inflammatory mechanism is well established. 2025 Inflammopharmacology review (NLRP3 inflammasomes pathway: a key target for Metformin, doi:10.1007/s10787-025-01702-4) summarizes multiple modulation routes: TLR4/NF-kB axis, FOXO3, NEK7, GSDMD; AMPK/PP2A in ox-LDL-stimulated macrophages (PMID 30851273); IL-1beta suppression in keratinocytes via SIRT1 (PMID 32398655 Cell Death Discov 2020); mitochondrial ATP / mtDNA-dependent NLRP3 activation (PMID 34107285 Immunity 2021). | CAVEAT: corpus extraction for this path (PMID 35466661) is an artifact -- it's a HCQ trial that only mentions metformin as background therapy. dpc=1 from that PMID does NOT support a mechanistic claim. The mechanism is validated by independent external evidence, not by this corpus extraction. Path retained as VALIDATED based on external evidence; corpus citation should be removed when extraction pipeline filter is applied.

pioglitazone -> inflammation.notes: Pioglitazone anti-inflammatory effect via PPAR-gamma is mechanistically established. PPAR-gamma agonism reduces availability of coactivators for NF-kB, thereby suppressing IL-1, IL-6, TNF-alpha, MCP-1, VCAM-1, IκBα transcription (PMID 19136609 PPARα/γ cross-talk paper, 2009 PMC2633943). 2025 Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism systematic review of pioglitazone add-on (Khan 2025, doi:10.1002/edm2.70061) notes anti-inflammatory contribution to CV benefit on top of HbA1c reduction. | CAVEAT: corpus extraction (PMID 35466661, matched_text='400 mg OD') is an artifact -- HCQ trial that uses pioglitazone as comparator. Mechanism is real but THIS corpus citation does not support it. Path validated on external evidence; extraction pipeline filter should drop this dpc=1 dose-fragment entry.

atorvastatin -> T2D.notes: Sattar 2010 (PMID 19794004) IPD meta of 13 trials, 91,140 pts: statins +9% incident T2D. Navarese 2016 NMA (PMID 27277934): atorvastatin specifically +12%, pravastatin neutral/protective. CTT 2024 Lancet D&E IPD meta: confirmed dose-dependent. CV benefits outweigh diabetogenic risk. Path direction: atorvastatin INCREASES T2D risk (not therapeutic). Flag for direction reversal in corpus. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified PMIDs: 19794004 (Sattar 2010 Lancet collaborative meta), 27277934 (Navarese 2016 NMA). Statins +9% T2D risk; atorvastatin specifically +12% in NMA. CV benefits outweigh diabetogenic risk per CTT IPD meta (Lancet D&E 2024, PMID pending verification). Path direction: atorvastatin INCREASES T2D risk (not therapeutic for T2D). Should consider flagging path-direction for review.

belatacept -> T1D.notes: Belatacept (LEA29Y, CTLA-4-Ig) used as calcineurin-sparing maintenance in islet transplant for T1D. PMID 37359825 (Posselt 2023 Transpl Int): 3/5 belatacept patients insulin-independent at 10y, HbA1c 7.1->5.8%. Limited to small CIT-04/08 cohort. Not a primary T1D therapy outside transplant. Mechanism plausible (CD28-B7 blockade) but no large RCT. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified: 37359825 (Posselt 2023 Transpl Int). | RE-AUDIT 2026-06-19: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. Fresh 2024-2025 lit (islet-transplant outcome reviews; 20-yr Italy single-centre Lancet D&E 2024; CNI-sparing immunosuppression review PMC10286829) shows NO new belatacept-specific T1D RCT. Field shifting to stem-cell-derived islets (zimislecel/VX-880) with varied immunosuppression. Belatacept remains CNI-sparing maintenance in islet transplant, not a primary T1D therapy. No rating change. | RE-AUDIT 2026-06-28: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. Web sweep found no belatacept-specific T1D RCT beyond CIT-04/08; most recent durable-outcome pub remains 2023 (Transpl Int 10.3389/ti.2023.11367, 60-70% insulin-independent at 10-13y incl operational tolerance off-IS). belatacept->islet_transplant stays VALIDATED; belatacept->T1D stays PARTIALLY (transplant-only, no primary-T1D-therapy RCT).
supporting_pmids_context: PMC10286829 (CNI-sparing immunosuppressive regimens in beta-cell replacement, review)

belatacept -> islet_transplant.notes: PMID 37359825 (Posselt 2023): belatacept-based calcineurin-sparing immunosuppression maintains long-term insulin independence in islet transplant. CIT-04/08 cohort. Better beta-cell preservation than CNI-based regimens. Validated. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified: 37359825.

oxidative_stress -> beta_cell.notes: Oxidative stress -> beta cell dysfunction is one of the most strongly supported mechanistic axes in diabetes. PMID 36246880 (Front Endocrinol 2022 'Oxidative stress-mediated beta cell death and dysfunction as a target for diabetes management', PMC9554708): beta cells express only ~5% of liver-cell antioxidant capacity (catalase, GPx, SOD) and are uniquely vulnerable. ROS drives loss of beta-cell identity transcription factors, dedifferentiation, and apoptosis. 2025 Chinese Medical Journal review 'Oxidative stress in diabetes mellitus and its complications' (doi:10.1097/CM9.0000000000003230) reaffirms ROS-NF-kB vicious cycle in beta-cell pathology. Mechanism is causally linked in T2D pathogenesis (glucotoxicity, lipotoxicity); RCT-level antioxidant interventions remain mixed but mechanism itself is canonical.

rapamycin -> islet_transplant.notes: Sirolimus is core component of Edmonton protocol (PMID 16968130 NEJM 2006 international trial). 5-yr insulin independence dropped to ~10%. Berney 2009 (PMID 18713146 Transpl Int): "friend or foe?" review of dual mechanisms. Sirolimus impairs GSIS, depletes ER Ca++, may reduce engraftment. Mixed evidence: needed for immunosuppression but has direct beta-cell toxicity. PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified: 18713146 (Berney 2009 friend-or-foe review). Edmonton NEJM 2006 international trial cited in search but PMID needs separate verification before recording.

rapamycin -> nephropathy.notes: Preclinical evidence robust: PMID 16597691 (Lloberas 2006 JASN): rapamycin slows DKD progression in rats; PMID 16364254 (Sakaguchi 2006 KI): attenuates renal hypertrophy via p70S6K. PMID 27338360 (Lieberthal 2016): mTOR pathway central to DKD. BUT clinical translation limited; in transplant setting, sirolimus + CNI may worsen pre-existing DKD per Shapiro CITR. PARTIALLY_VALIDATED -- preclinical strong, clinical mixed. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified: 16597691 (Lloberas JASN 2006), 16364254 (Sakaguchi 2006 KI), 27338360 (Lieberthal 2016). | RE-AUDIT 2026-06-19: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. Fresh search returned only the same mechanistic/preclinical studies already cited (16597691, 27338360) plus the 2016 IJMS review; NO new 2024-2026 clinical RCT of mTOR inhibition for diabetic kidney disease. Preclinical strong, clinical translation still limited/mixed (sirolimus+CNI may worsen pre-existing DKD in transplant). No rating change.

empagliflozin -> nephropathy.validation_notes: EMPA-KIDNEY (Herrington et al. NEJM 2023, PMID 36331190): RCT n=6,609 CKD patients, empagliflozin 10mg/d, primary composite (kidney progression or CV death) HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.64-0.82, p<0.000001); 28% relative risk reduction confirmed across eGFR strata. Effect persisted post-trial. Validated via 2026-05-12 web search.

canagliflozin -> inflammation.validation_notes: CANVAS post-hoc mediation analysis (Sen et al. Diabetes Obes Metab 2022, PMID 35635326): canagliflozin in T2D reduced urinary KIM-1, TNFR-1, TNFR-2 and MCP-1; reduction in tubular inflammation partly mediated benefit. CANVAS primary publication (Neal et al. NEJM 2017, PMID 28605608) provides core trial context. SGLT2i class systematic review (23 studies, n=1,654) shows hsCRP reduction independent of HbA1c. VALIDATED. Cross-validated 2026-05-12.

oxidative_stress -> T1D.notes: Oxidative stress contributes to T1D beta-cell destruction via both direct injury (beta cells have low antioxidant capacity) and immune amplification: ROS converts M2 -> M1 macrophages; NO/peroxynitrite from infiltrating immune cells damage islets; oxidative post-translational modifications of insulin create neo-antigens recognized by autoreactive T cells (Frontiers Immunology 2025 'oxidative post-translational modifications in T1D pathogenesis'). Mitochondria are involved in both the target beta-cells and the attacking T cells. PMID 21647409 (Chen 2011 Antioxid Redox Signal) reviews redox modulation potential in T1D. RATED PARTIALLY_VALIDATED rather than VALIDATED because mechanistic plausibility is strong but RCT-level antioxidant trials (e.g., nicotinamide ENDIT, vitamin E) have NOT shown T1D prevention or beta-cell preservation. Pathway is real; therapeutic translation remains negative.

NLRP3_inflammasome -> T2D.notes: Strongly validated mechanistic link. PMID 34536551 (Karasawa 2021 Cardiovasc Res) reviews NLRP3 in T2D/atherosclerosis. PMID 17554302 (Larsen NEJM 2007): anakinra (IL-1RA) improved beta-cell function in T2D in 13-wk RCT -- proof of concept for IL-1beta pathway. NLRP3-IL-1beta-IRS axis disrupts insulin signaling. Donath group ongoing T2D inflammasome trials. Mechanism: obesity activates NLRP3 in adipose macrophages -> IL-1beta -> IRS serine phosphorylation -> insulin resistance. | PMID AUDIT 2026-05-13: Verified: 34536551 (Karasawa 2021 review). Anakinra NEJM 2007 (Larsen) cited but PMID not directly confirmed in search; mechanistic link well-supported by multiple reviews.

Treg_expansion -> T1D.validation_notes: 2026-06-13 web re-validation: Treg expansion is mechanistically real but clinical beta-cell preservation NOT robustly demonstrated. T-Rex phase 2 RCT (PMID 38718135, Sci Transl Med 2024): single-dose autologous polyclonal expanded Tregs were SAFE but did NOT preserve residual beta-cell function vs placebo. 2025 systematic review & meta-analysis (PMID 41267047, BMC Endocr Disord, 19 studies) found a paradoxical dissociation -- immunotherapy/low-dose IL-2 expands Tregs and can preserve C-peptide as a biomarker without consistent HbA1c benefit. Remains PARTIALLY_VALIDATED: target engagement (Treg expansion) confirmed; durable clinical beta-cell preservation from Treg expansion alone unproven.

rituximab -> T1D.validation_notes: Pescovitz NEJM 2009 + Diabetes Care 2014 2-yr extension: rituximab delays C-peptide loss ~8 mo but does not arrest beta-cell decline.

rituximab -> nephropathy.validation_notes: Path is a co-occurrence artifact from PMID 19940299 (Pescovitz NEJM 2009 — rituximab in new-onset T1D), where "diabetic nephropathy" is mentioned only as a T1D complication, NOT as a treatment indication for rituximab. Web validation 2026-05-03: rituximab is well-established for MEMBRANOUS NEPHROPATHY (PMID 35074299: meta-analysis of 11 trials, n=723, significant remission improvement) and other primary glomerular diseases (minimal change, lupus nephritis), but NOT for diabetic kidney disease. Multiple membranous nephropathy trials specifically EXCLUDE diabetic patients to avoid confounding. No RCT or systematic review evidence supports rituximab in diabetic nephropathy. RECOMMENDATION: drop this path from drug-repurposing dashboards or label explicitly as "membranous nephropathy (non-diabetic)" with a separate path. The rituximab -> T1D and rituximab -> beta_cell paths remain PARTIALLY_VALIDATED.

rituximab -> beta_cell.validation_notes: Pescovitz NEJM 2009 (PMID 19940299): single course of rituximab in new-onset T1D significantly preserved C-peptide AUC vs placebo at 12 months, lower HbA1c, less insulin. Pescovitz Diabetes Care 2014 2-yr follow-up (PMID 24026563): rate of C-peptide decline by 24-30 months parallels controls; cumulative effect = 8.2-month delay in beta-cell decline; effect wanes — does not arrest underlying autoimmunity. Beese BMC Medicine 2025 NMA (PMID 40598585): rituximab is among 11/42 interventions with significantly higher C-peptide at 12 months vs placebo, but ranks below teplizumab and low-dose ATG in cross-trial comparisons. Conclusion: rituximab partially preserves beta-cell function transiently but does not arrest beta-cell destruction. Effect is real but modest and time-limited. PARTIALLY_VALIDATED: same evidence base as rituximab -> T1D path.

teplizumab -> T1D.validation_notes: Teplizumab delays progression from Stage 2 to Stage 3 T1D by a median of ~2 years (Herold et al. NEJM 2019, PMID 31180194; TN-10 extended follow-up) and preserves C-peptide / reduces HbA1c in newly diagnosed T1D (PROTECT NEJM 2023, PMID 37865119). 2025-2026 real-world data replicate the signal: Diabetologia 2025 (DOI 10.1007/s00125-025-06646-6, 30 treated vs 10 controls), Mahesh et al. Diabetes Obesity & Metabolism 2026 (DOI 10.1111/dom.70354, only ~17% of 42 Stage 2 cases progressed to insulin in first year), and PMID 39949173 (2025 caregiver/adult real-world experiences). A meta-analysis of 8 RCTs (n=754) reports preserved C-peptide, reduced HbA1c, and insulin-initiation delay up to 24 months. Confidence HIGH. | RE-VALIDATED 2026-08-11 (long-term follow-up angle): TN-10 Extension (ADA 2025 abstract db25-840-P, DOI 10.2337/db25-840-P) followed former TN-10 participants who progressed to Stage 3 — reaffirms delay-of-progression signal; PROTECT Extension (NCT04598893, observational, no drug) ongoing for long-term safety/durability. C-peptide preservation solid at yrs 1-2 (one or two courses); durability BEYOND 2 yrs remains an OPEN question per 2025-26 reviews. Status stays VALIDATED (HIGH) for 0-2yr; long-term durability = partially established/open. Next revalidate ~2026-09-11.

teplizumab -> autoimmune.validation_notes: TN-10 (Herold et al. NEJM 2019, PMID 31180194): teplizumab 14-day course in stage 2 T1D relatives delayed median progression to stage 3 by ~24 months (HR 0.41); basis for 2022 FDA approval. PROTECT phase 3 (Ramos et al. NEJM 2023, PMID 37889505, n=328 stage 3 newly-diagnosed): stimulated C-peptide LSM difference +0.13 pmol/mL at week 78 (p<0.001), preserving beta cell function. VALIDATED. Cross-validated 2026-05-12.

Short-term IV data strongest (NATHAN, SYDNEY trials); long-term oral data more mixed. Symptom improvement consistent. HIGH confidence for symptom modification, MEDIUM for disease modification.

SGLT2i_NLRP3_DKD.mechanism: SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin) reduce NLRP3 inflammasome activation in renal tubular cells via (a) beta-hydroxybutyrate-induced NLRP3 inhibition, (b) accumulation of TCA-cycle immunometabolite itaconate, and (c) reduced RIP1-RIP3-MLKL-mediated necroinflammation, leading to decreased IL-1beta/IL-18/NLRP3 expression and attenuated renal fibrosis.
SGLT2i_NLRP3_DKD.clinical_anchor: Downstream kidney-outcome benefit of SGLT2i is established in large trials (CREDENCE, DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY; see Lancet 2022 collaborative meta-analysis, PMID 36351458). NLRP3-axis remains the most parsimonious mechanistic explanation but has NOT been proven to mediate the clinical effect in humans.

caveats: All direct mechanistic evidence is preclinical (mouse UUO model, HK-2 cells, rat STZ DKD).
No randomized clinical trial in humans has directly measured NLRP3 inflammasome activity as a mediator of SGLT2i renal benefit.
Effect size on NLRP3 read-outs varies by model (UUO vs STZ vs db/db).
SGLT2i_NLRP3_DKD.validation_notes: Multiple independent 2022-2025 preclinical studies show dapagliflozin inhibits NLRP3 activation in fibrotic/diabetic kidneys via metabolic (itaconate, BHB) and necroptotic mechanisms. Narrative reviews in Braz J Nephrol (2024) and Nutrients (2023) converge on same mechanism. Clinical DKD benefit of SGLT2i well-established separately; NLRP3 is a plausible but unproven human mediator.

Gap remains GOLD: as new modalities (encapsulated, gene-edited, allogeneic stem-cell-derived) enter trials, the IR question deserves prospective measurement. Next audit: 2026-06-06.

BHB_to_NLRP3_inhibition.mechanism: β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome assembly by blocking K+ efflux and ASC oligomerization; independent of UCP2/Sirt2/Gpr109a/HDAC. SGLT2i raise serum BHB, providing a candidate mechanistic link to NLRP3 suppression in DKD/CV outcomes.

external_pmids.25686106: Youm et al. Nat Med 2015 — foundational: BHB blocks NLRP3-mediated disease (cell+mouse).
external_pmids.28794421: Yamanashi et al. Sci Rep 2017 — BHB endogenic NLRP3 inhibitor; anti-inflammatory in stress model.
external_pmids.32358544: Kim et al. Nat Commun 2020 — SGLT2i in T2D+CVD pts: ↑BHB, ↓insulin, ↓NLRP3-IL-1β in human macrophages (30-day RCT vs SU).
external_pmids.34918381: Front Pharmacol/Ke 2022 — already in library; SGLT2i↔NLRP3 via itaconate (alternate axis).
external_pmids.39412512: Braz J Nephrol 2024 — SGLT2i+NLRP3 in DKD review (already in library).
external_pmids.40055596: BMC Nephrology 2025 review (Li et al; s12882-025-04019-0) - KD/BHB delays DKD progression via anti-inflammation (incl. NLRP3), anti-oxidative-stress, anti-fibrosis, autophagy. Captures the previously-uncaptured 2025 BMC Nephrology source.
external_pmids.40793083: Liu et al, J Diabetes 2025 (PMC12340978) - MULTI-COHORT (NHANES cross-sectional + West China T2DM-DKD longitudinal Cox/RCS + Mendelian randomization): elevated circulating beta-OHB INDEPENDENTLY associated with REDUCED ESRD risk (nonlinear; high-normal BHB may delay DKD progression). First human hard-renal-outcome + MR support for the BHB->renal-protection link.

caveats: Most BHB→NLRP3 evidence is in vitro / mouse models. The in-human Kim 2020 study is a pharmacodynamic biomarker readout, not a clinical-outcome RCT.
BHB rise from SGLT2i is modest (typically 0.1–0.5 mmol/L) — whether this magnitude is sufficient to produce clinically meaningful NLRP3 inhibition in humans remains unproven.
2025 BMC Nephrology review (Springer; PMID not yet captured) and 2025 ADA abstract 389-P (BHB mitigates DKD) are non-PMID/abstract-only sources, so weight cautiously.
Alternative mechanisms (itaconate, RIP1-RIP3-MLKL, TXNIP-NLRP3) ALSO proposed for SGLT2i — BHB is not the sole or proven dominant axis.

2025 mechanistic PREPRINT (bioRxiv 2025.05.01.650510, Univ Vermont; NOT peer-reviewed, NO PMID - weight cautiously): NLRP3 inhibition is manifested only by the ACID form (beta-hydroxybutyric acid) or in an acidic microenvironment; sodium-BHB and NaOH-neutralized BHBA do NOT inhibit NLRP3. Implication: modest, physiological-pH serum BHB elevations from SGLT2i may be insufficient to engage NLRP3 - tempers the linear SGLT2i->BHB->NLRP3 translation story (mechanistic linearity DOWN even as human outcome association is UP).
BHB_to_NLRP3_inhibition.recommendation: Add an explicit "BHB→NLRP3" path entry in research_paths.json next pipeline rebuild; flag SGLT2i→NLRP3 as having multiple proposed mechanisms (BHB, itaconate, TXNIP-NLRP3) rather than a single linear story.

TXNIP_NLRP3_beta_cell_DKD.mechanism: High glucose drives ROS, TXNIP dissociates from thioredoxin and binds NLRP3, triggering inflammasome assembly and IL-1beta. Operates in BOTH pancreatic beta cells (pyroptosis) and renal mesangial/podocyte cells (DKD), a shared TXNIP/NLRP3 axis.

verapamil_txnip_beta_cell_t1d.path_name: Verapamil -> TXNIP suppression -> beta cell preservation (T1D)
verapamil_txnip_beta_cell_t1d.rationale: Two independent RCTs confirm sustained C-peptide preservation. Ovalle 2018 (Nat Med, NCT02372253, n=24 completers, adults) showed verapamil improved MMTT-stimulated C-peptide AUC at both 3 and 12 months (prespecified primary endpoint), with lower insulin requirement increase and fewer hypoglycemic events. Forlenza CLVer trial 2023 (JAMA, n=88 pediatric ages 7-17) showed C-peptide 30% higher at 52 weeks vs placebo, with 95% vs 71% retaining peak C-peptide >=0.2 pmol/mL. Both trials used similar dosing and endpoint timing. Mechanism (TXNIP suppression) consistent with preclinical literature. AEs comparable to placebo.
verapamil_txnip_beta_cell_t1d.caveats: Both trials are short-term (12 months). The 2022 follow-up exploratory work (Nat Commun, Ovalle group) showed broader systemic effects but did not establish durability beyond 1 year. Ver-A-T1D protocol (PMC11605811) is a multicenter RCT still enrolling - longer-term durability and any disease-modification beyond C-peptide preservation remain open.
verapamil_txnip_beta_cell_t1d.revisit_2026_07_09: DOWNGRADED VALIDATED->PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. Ver-A-T1D (Pieber/Graz; n=136 adults, 21 sites, 6 EU countries; recruitment completed May 2024), the largest and most rigorous independent ADULT replication, reported a NEUTRAL primary at EASD 2025 (Vienna, Sep 2025): NO significant C-peptide (AUC) difference vs placebo at 12 months in ITT, and no difference at 3/6/9 months. This directly contradicts the positive adult signal from the smaller Ovalle 2018 trial (n=24 completers, PMID 29988125). The pediatric CLVer RCT (Forlenza JAMA 2023, n=88, PMID 36826844) remains positive at 52 weeks, and the TXNIP/L-type-Ca-channel mechanism is robust in preclinical work. Net: mechanism sound; pediatric preservation replicated; adult efficacy now UNCERTAIN after a well-powered negative primary. 2-yr AUC and an open-label extension (>3yr) are planned for Ver-A-T1D. As of Jul 2026 the EASD result appears conference-presented; peer-reviewed full publication not yet confirmed.

external_refs_2026.EASD2025_Ver-A-T1D: Pieber et al., Ver-A-T1D primary results presented EASD 2025 (news-medical 20250918; healio 20250924) - neutral 12-mo C-peptide.

rituximab -> T1D.evidence: Pescovitz NEJM 2009 (PMID 19940299): RCT n=87, 4-dose rituximab vs placebo in newly diagnosed T1D. At 1 year, rituximab group had significantly higher C-peptide AUC, lower HbA1c, lower insulin requirements vs placebo. 2-year extension Pescovitz Diabetes Care 2014 (PMID 24026563): rate of C-peptide decline became parallel to placebo after ~8.2-month delay; effect transient. Conclusion: rituximab DELAYS but does not arrest beta-cell loss in recent-onset T1D. PARTIALLY_VALIDATED — real but limited durable benefit.
rituximab -> T1D.caveat: Effect plateaus by 30 months; no evidence of disease modification beyond delayed C-peptide loss. Underlying autoimmunity not arrested.

rituximab -> T1D.revisit_note: 2026-07-14 reaffirmed PARTIAL: Rituximab delays C-peptide decline ~8.2 mo at 1 yr (NEJM 2009 PMID 19940299) and effect persists to 2 yr (Diabetes Care 2014 PMID 24026563 / PMC6410357), but extended follow-up shows benefit disappears by ~30 mo (decline parallels placebo) — B-cell depletion alone does not alter underlying pathophysiology. No net-new RCT/SR since last check. Rating unchanged.
rituximab -> T1D.reaffirm_note: 2026-07-29: PARTIALLY_VALIDATED reaffirmed & strengthened. 2025 systematic review + network meta-analysis (PMC12211534; 60 RCTs, 4597 pts, 32 intervention classes, searches to 2024-07-31) confirms rituximab partially preserves 1-yr C-peptide but ranks below low-dose ATG/teplizumab; benefit transient (~8.2-mo delay in decline, parallels placebo by 30 mo). NEW: NCT07041268 (2025) testing REPEATED rituximab courses in adolescents — directly probes whether re-dosing addresses the known transience. No evidence yet of durable disease modification. Status unchanged: real but limited durable benefit.

rituximab -> beta_cell.key_finding: Rituximab transiently preserves C-peptide (~8 mo delay in decline at 1-2 yr) but effect wanes; B-cell depletion alone insufficient to arrest beta-cell loss.
rituximab -> beta_cell.revisit_note: Reaffirmed by 2 fresh 2025 syntheses: BMC Medicine network meta-analysis (10.1186/s12916-025-04201-z) ranks low-dose ATG & teplizumab ABOVE rituximab for 1-2yr C-peptide preservation; BMC Endocrine Disorders SR/MA (10.1186/s12902-025-02088-8, PMC12636228) shows 'paradoxical dissociation' between beta-cell preservation and glycemic control across immunomodulators. Rituximab effect modest & transient, wanes after 1yr. No upgrade.
rituximab -> beta_cell.revisit_2026_06_22: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. Web sweep returned only pre-2026 evidence: NEJMoa0904452 (PMID 19940299, 1-yr partial preservation), Diabetes Care 2014 2-yr results (PMID 24026563) showing 8.2-mo delay in C-peptide decline that then parallels placebo. Comparative MA still ranks rituximab BELOW low-dose ATG & teplizumab. No new 2026 RCT/MA. No upgrade.
rituximab -> beta_cell.revisit_note_2026_07_04: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED. 2025 BMC Medicine network meta-analysis (PMC12211534 / doi 10.1186/s12916-025-04201-z; 60 RCTs, 4597 pts, lit through 2024-07-31) reports 11 interventions with significantly higher 12-mo C-peptide than placebo - rituximab/anti-CD20 is NOT among them; anti-CD20 effect described as transient (patients eventually progress). Landmark Pescovitz NEJM 2009 (PMC6410357) positive at 1yr but wanes. No upgrade - effect modest/transient, does not arrest beta-cell loss.
rituximab -> beta_cell.revisit_2026_07_23: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED (Thu run). Web sweep: 12-mo C-peptide preservation confirmed (Pescovitz NEJM 2009, PMID 19940299); effect transient - Diabetes Care 2014 2-yr results (PMID 24026563) show ~8.2-mo delay then decline parallels placebo as CD19+ B-cells recover (~69% baseline by 1yr). 2025 network MA (PMC12211534) lists 11 interventions beating placebo at 12-mo C-peptide; anti-CD20/rituximab NOT among top performers (teplizumab, baricitinib, cyclosporin lead). No new 2026 rituximab RCT/MA. No upgrade.
rituximab -> beta_cell.revisit_2026_08_12: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED (Wed run). Fresh web sweep: no new completed 2026 rituximab RCT/MA. Core evidence unchanged - Pescovitz NEJM 2009 (PMID 19940299, NEJMoa0904452/PMC6410357) partial 12-mo C-peptide preservation; 2-yr wane (PMID 24026563); 2025 network MA PMC12211534 (60 RCTs) still excludes anti-CD20/rituximab from the 11 interventions beating placebo at 12-mo. NEW: an ongoing Phase 2 rituximab-pvvr +/- SEQUENTIAL abatacept combo trial (rituximab wk1-4, abatacept from wk16 x20mo) aims to enhance durability - NO results yet. No upgrade; effect remains modest/transient.

rituximab -> nephropathy (DIABETIC).key_finding: No clinical evidence supports rituximab for diabetic nephropathy. The path is a co-occurrence artifact. Rituximab IS validated for membranous nephropathy (PMID 35074299 meta-analysis), but that is a distinct, autoimmune-mediated glomerular disease — NOT diabetic kidney disease.
rituximab -> nephropathy (DIABETIC).reaffirm_note: 2026-07-17: CONTRADICTED reaffirmed. Fresh search returns rituximab RCT evidence only for IgA nephropathy (negative: no proteinuria/eGFR benefit, PMID 27821627) and membranous nephropathy (positive, distinct autoimmune GN); NO diabetic-nephropathy RCT. Path remains a co-occurrence artifact.

dapagliflozin_nephropathy.evidence_summary: DAPA-CKD landmark RCT (NEJM 2020 PMID 32970396, n=4304): dapagliflozin 10 mg vs placebo over median 2.4 y reduced composite (sustained ≥50% eGFR decline, ESKD, renal or CV death) HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.51-0.72). Confirmed by 2024 SR/MA (PMC11370938, 9 RCTs, ~30k participants) showing OR 0.61 (0.57-0.65) for primary kidney composite and OR 0.69 (0.63-0.76) for mortality, with UACR reduction of -23.99% (95% CI -34.82 to -13.15). Effect present in patients with and without T2D. Mechanism strongly supported. | 2026-07-18 reaffirmation: NDT 2024 time-to-event analysis (McEwan et al., PMID 38730538, DOI 10.1093/ndt/gfae106) using DAPA-CKD patient-level data projects dapagliflozin delays time to kidney failure by 6.6 y (25.2 vs 18.5 y), plus delays to all-cause mortality, sustained eGFR decline, and HF hospitalization — strengthens durability of the renoprotective signal. Rating unchanged VALIDATED (STRONG).
dapagliflozin_nephropathy.note: Duplicate of 'dapagliflozin -> nephropathy' (VALIDATED via DAPA-CKD, PMID 32862232/35364937). Status reconciled 2026-06-18.

dapagliflozin_T2D.evidence_summary: Landmark indication for dapagliflozin in T2D — VALIDATED. DECLARE-TIMI 58 (NEJM 2019, PMID 30415602; n=17,160 T2D patients, median 4.2 y follow-up): dapagliflozin 10 mg vs placebo MET non-inferiority for MACE (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.84-1.03; p=0.17 for superiority) and was SUPERIOR for the co-primary composite of CV death/HF hospitalization (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.73-0.95; p=0.005), driven primarily by HF-hospitalization reduction (HR 0.73). Cardiorenal secondary composite (Mosenzon Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2019, PMID 31196815): HR 0.76 (0.67-0.87); renal-specific composite excluding CV death HR 0.53 (0.43-0.66). Effect consistent in patients with and without established CVD; benefit present in preserved-EF and reduced-EF subgroups. Multi-trial SGLT2i SR/MA (Zelniker Lancet 2019; updated 2024-2025 meta-analyses) places DECLARE alongside EMPA-REG, CANVAS, CREDENCE, EMPEROR, DAPA-HF, DAPA-CKD as collectively defining SGLT2i benefit in T2D for cardio-renal outcomes. ADA Standards of Care 2025 list dapagliflozin as guideline-recommended in T2D with established/at-risk CVD, HF, or CKD. | 2026-07-18 reaffirmation: no contradicting evidence; SGLT2i cardiorenal benefit remains ADA-guideline-standard. Linked kidney-outcome durability further supported by NDT 2024 time-to-event analysis (PMID 38730538). Rating unchanged VALIDATED (STRONG).
caveats: DAPA-HF and DAPA-CKD established benefit in patients without diabetes too — the dapagliflozin->T2D label has expanded into broader cardiorenal indications.

DECLARE was not powered for kidney hard endpoints (kidney-specific composite a secondary analysis); DAPA-CKD provides the dedicated kidney-outcome RCT (already validated separately as dapagliflozin_nephropathy).

verapamil_T1D.mechanism: Verapamil blocks L-type Ca channels, lowering intracellular Ca, which suppresses TXNIP transcription and reduces glucotoxicity-driven beta-cell apoptosis (TXNIP overexpression is essential for glucose-induced beta-cell death).

external_evidence.Xu 2023 Diabetes 72(10):1460: Verapamil prevents decline of IGF-I, promotes beta-cell IGF-I signaling in T1D.
external_evidence.Ovalle/Shalev 2018 Nat Med adult RCT: Earlier positive adult RCT - verapamil preserved C-peptide at 12mo.
external_evidence.Ver-A-T1D adult RCT (EASD 2025, Pieber;: 136 adults new-onset T1D, SR-verapamil 360mg vs placebo 12mo. PRIMARY 2h-MMTT C-peptide AUC NOT significantly different at 3/6/9/12mo; non-significant trend favoring verapamil. NEGATIVE primary. Confirmed 2026-07-04 via EASD 2025 readout + News-Medical 2025-09-18 + Diabetes UK + HRA study summary. Specific Diabetologia journal DOI still NOT independently confirmable via web - primary appears conference-presented, peer-reviewed journal pub not yet verified. Cite EASD 2025 + news, NOT the DOI, until confirmed.

verapamil_T1D.note: DOWNGRADE: largest European RCT (Ver-A-T1D) missed primary endpoint; clinical efficacy now MIXED (one positive, one null adult RCT). Mechanism remains strong. Watch Ver-A-T1D full journal pub (queued) and pediatric NCT07199946.

Heterogeneity by age/onset confirmed. Status unchanged PARTIALLY_VALIDATED.

Diabetologia DOI remains UNVERIFIED (flagged since 2026-07-02) - not fabricated by us, originally supplied but never independently reconfirmed; sourcing shifted to verifiable EASD/news references.

Adult Ver-A-T1D primary re-confirmed NEGATIVE via EASD 2025 + Breakthrough T1D EASD-2025 recap + News-Medical 2025-09-18: no significant 2h-MMTT C-peptide difference vs placebo at 12mo, non-significant trend favoring verapamil. sources.finding: 14% RRR in 3-point MACE vs placebo (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.74-0.99); 38% reduction in CV death (HR 0.62); 35% reduction in HF hospitalization (HR 0.65) over 3.1 yr in T2D with established CV disease (n=7,020).
Kidney disease progression or CV death 13.1% vs 16.9% (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.64-0.82, p<0.001) in CKD with or without diabetes (n=6,609).
Empagliflozin reduced composite CV death/HF hospitalization 25% in HFrEF; benefit extends to non-diabetic HF.

empagliflozin_cv_hf_ckd.notes: Three independent landmark RCTs from regulatory-quality sources; effect sizes consistent across CV/HF/CKD endpoints. | 2026-07-21: reaffirmed VALIDATED; EMPEROR-Reduced PMID filled (32865377); added 3 2025-2026 confirming SR/MA; no reversal.

Empagliflozin IPD meta-analysis of acute+chronic kidney outcomes, Lancet Diab Endocrinol 2025 (PIIS2213-8587(25)00222-0): benefit irrespective of acute eGFR dip.
Bahardoust et al 2026 SR/MA (Endocrinol Diabetes Metab, doi:10.1002/edm2.70203): empagliflozin reduces CKD outcomes in established-CVD patients.

glp1_ra_cv_outcomes.notes: LEADER (liraglutide, PMID 27295427, NEJM 2016): MACE HR 0.87 (0.78-0.97). SUSTAIN-6 (s.c. semaglutide, PMID 27633186, NEJM 2016): MACE HR 0.74 (0.58-0.95). PIONEER 6 (oral semaglutide, PMID 31185157, NEJM 2019): MACE HR 0.79 (0.57-1.11), met noninferiority. REWIND (dulaglutide): MACE reduction in primary prevention. 2024 meta-analysis (PMID 38953365) MACE reduction confirmed across patients with and without diabetes. Class effect supported.
glp1_ra_cv_outcomes.caveats: REWIND population had only 31.5% with CVD vs ~70% in others; heterogeneity in dosing and follow-up duration; trial-level analyses not at individual patient level except IPD subset.
glp1_ra_cv_outcomes.revisit_2026-07-26: Re-validated (stalest path, prior 2026-05-08). STRENGTHENED. SOUL trial (PMID 40162642, NEJM 2025-03-29): oral semaglutide in T2D with ASCVD/CKD, MACE HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.77-0.96), P=0.0028 over median 47.5 mo -- upgrades oral-semaglutide evidence from PIONEER 6 noninferiority to demonstrated superiority; nonfatal MI driver (-26%). Supported by 2025 JACC SR/MA of 99,599 patients across 21 trials (10.1016/j.jacc.2025.08.027) confirming consistent class-level MACE benefit incl. non-diabetic obesity (~20% MACE reduction). Rating unchanged: VALIDATED (robust class effect).

tegoprubart_islet_t1d.source: ATTD 2025 conference + Eledon press releases + Transplantation 2025 abstract 04-3
tegoprubart_islet_t1d.caveats: NOT YET PEER-REVIEWED. Single-center investigator-initiated trial of 12 pts at UChicago; 10 evaluable >4 weeks reportedly insulin-independent with HbA1c <6.0%. CRITICAL: claims of "no rejection episodes" and "no de novo DSAs" are conference/press-release framing exactly mirroring the doctrine red flag for "zero rejection" overclaiming. Short follow-up. Press-release conclusions should NOT be cited as VETTED evidence in dashboards. Re-audit when peer-reviewed publication appears.

STILL conference/press-release only - NO peer-reviewed journal publication located. The "no rejection / no DSA" framing continues to mirror the doctrine "zero rejection" red flag; do NOT propagate as validated. Awaiting peer-reviewed publication (queue item, next check 2026-08-02).

Eledon UChicago IIT still 12/12 insulin-independent, mean recent HbA1c ~5.4%, no rejection/no de novo DSA (source: Eledon IR press release, HCPLive, Breakthrough T1D, presented ADA 86th Sci Sessions Jun-2026, New Orleans, Witkowski). teplizumab_long_term_followup.notes: PROTECT primary (NEJMoa2308743, NEJM 2023, n~300 peds 8-17, 2:1) = significant preservation of stimulated C-peptide at wk78 vs placebo. LONG-TERM: PROTECT Extension (NCT04598893) OBSERVATIONAL, q6mo through Month 42 (60mo combined); as of 2026-08-09 NO peer-reviewed long-term extension readout published (clinicaltrials.gov + HRA + UF/UCSF pages only). TN-10 prevention (STM 2021, scitranslmed.abc8980) supports durability. Rating: mid-term VALIDATED (RCT); long-term durability PENDING publication.

golimumab_t1d_beta_cell.source: T1GER phase 2 RCT primary (Quattrin et al, NEJM 2020; PMID 33207093) + 2-yr follow-up (Rigby et al, Diabetes Care 2023; PMID 36576974) + NMA (PMID 40598585).
golimumab_t1d_beta_cell.trial_name: T1GER (A Study of SIMPONI to Arrest Beta-Cell Loss in Type 1 Diabetes)
golimumab_t1d_beta_cell.key_results: n=84 (56 golimumab vs 28 placebo, 2:1), age 6-21 yrs new-onset T1D within 100 d of randomization, 52-week subcutaneous treatment. Primary: 4-h C-peptide AUC at week 52 0.64 vs 0.43 pmol/mL (mean diff 0.21, P<0.001). Off-therapy benefits persisted through 2 years (PMID 36576974).
golimumab_t1d_beta_cell.caveats: Phase 2; not powered for long-term safety. No phase 3 confirmation. NMA reported substantial heterogeneity across 60 trials/42 interventions.
golimumab_t1d_beta_cell.reaffirm_note: Re-validated 2026-07-28: T1GER phase 2 (Quattrin et al., NEJM 2020, PMID 33207093) 4h C-peptide AUC 0.64 vs 0.43 pmol/mL p<0.001, lower insulin use; 2-yr off-therapy follow-up (Diabetes Care 2023;46(3):561, PMID 36576974) continued metabolic benefit. Anti-TNF beta-cell preservation in new-onset T1D VALIDATED.

baricitinib_t1d_beta_cell.source: BANDIT phase 2 RCT primary publication (Waibel et al, NEJM 2023; PMID 38055252) + protocol (PMID 35606820) + NMA (PMID 40598585).
baricitinib_t1d_beta_cell.trial_name: BANDIT (Investigating the efficacy of baricitinib in new-onset T1D)
baricitinib_t1d_beta_cell.key_results: n=91 (60 baricitinib 4 mg/d vs 31 placebo), age 10-30 yrs, 48-week treatment. Primary endpoint mixed-meal-stimulated mean C-peptide AUC at week 48: 0.65 vs 0.43 nmol/L/min (P=0.001). HbA1c and exogenous insulin use also favored treatment.
baricitinib_t1d_beta_cell.notes: Primary trial publication now ingested. Mechanism: JAK1/JAK2 inhibition reduces IFN-gamma signaling and Th1/Th17 cytokine output. | 2026-07-27 reaffirmed VALIDATED via Monday web sweep: BANDIT phase-2 NEJM result (mixed-meal C-peptide 0.65 vs 0.43 nmol/L/min at 48 wk, n=91) re-confirmed. Breakthrough T1D/TrialNet note TWO phase-3 disease-modifying trials of baricitinib now underway; rating unchanged (single phase-2 RCT pending phase-3 replication).
baricitinib_t1d_beta_cell.caveats: Single phase 2 RCT; long-term safety in T1D and durability of effect after stopping treatment not yet established. Sponsor: Australian researchers; needs replication.

PMID 26589253 (Asian post-metformin RCT)

PMC6441028 (monotherapy MA, Sci Rep 2019)
PMC12106948 (add-on met+dapa MA)
pioglitazone -> T2D.corpus_artifact_2026-08-15: PMID 35466661 = Dutta D et al., J Postgrad Med 2022;68(2):85-92, HCQ-in-T2DM systematic review & meta-analysis (11 RCTs, n=2723). Its trial-characteristics table lists comparator/background drugs with dose strings, which the extractor converted into spurious drug->outcome edges. Discovered 2026-08-15 to affect 5 paths, not the 3 recorded in 2026-05-14. dpc=3 was inflated: all 3 claims are dose fragments from PMID 35466661 and TWO ARE THE IDENTICAL STRING '400 mg OD' (duplicate counted twice). External MA validation (PMC2701605 / PMC6441028 / PMC12106948) is independent and still stands - rating unchanged.

Suppresses IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α via AMPK + NF-κB inhibition
metformin -> inflammation.reaffirm_note: 2026-07-15 web recheck: reaffirmed VALIDATED. Added PMID 31182921 (Metformin inhibits NLRP3 via AMPK/mTOR, diabetic cardiomyopathy, IJBS 2019, preclinical). 2025-2026 NLRP3-diabetes reviews (PMC12395217) consistent. Mechanism = preclinical/mechanistic + limited clinical (myeloid caspase-1/IL-1b); no metformin RCT with NLRP3 clinical endpoint.
metformin -> inflammation.corpus_artifact_2026-08-15: PMID 35466661 = Dutta D et al., J Postgrad Med 2022;68(2):85-92, HCQ-in-T2DM systematic review & meta-analysis (11 RCTs, n=2723). Its trial-characteristics table lists comparator/background drugs with dose strings, which the extractor converted into spurious drug->outcome edges. Discovered 2026-08-15 to affect 5 paths, not the 3 recorded in 2026-05-14. External validation (PMID 31182921, NLRP3/AMPK) is INDEPENDENT and still stands - rating unchanged. Only the corpus-side dpc=1 is an artifact.

pioglitazone -> inflammation.downgrade_reason: Two independent problems found 2026-08-15. (a) CLAIM SCOPE: the stored external claim 'PPARgamma activation reduces hs-CRP, IL-6, TNF-alpha independently of glucose lowering' is only partly supported. The largest T2DM-specific pooled analysis (PMID 25897968, 27 RCTs) finds hsCRP and MCP-1 significantly reduced, but IL-6 NOT significant; MMP-9, sCD40L, PAI-1 and ICAM-1 also null. For pioglitazone specifically the authors state it 'reduced serum hsCRP and MCP-1 but had no marked effects on MMP-9, IL-6 and ICAM-1'. PAI-1/vWF/fibrinogen reductions were ROSIGLITAZONE-specific, not pioglitazone. The MA's own conclusion is 'limited evidence'. TNF-alpha was not a pooled endpoint at all - that claim traced to no source. (b) CORPUS SUPPORT IS AN ARTIFACT: the single corpus data point (PMID 35466661) is a hydroxychloroquine SR/MA in which pioglitazone appears only as a comparator-arm dose label ('400 mg OD'). No pioglitazone anti-inflammatory result exists in that paper.
pioglitazone -> inflammation.corpus_note: EXTRACTION ARTIFACT - comparator-arm dose fragment from PMID 35466661 (HCQ SR/MA). Zero real corpus support. Now dropped by the build_research_paths.py dose-fragment filter.

external_pmids.25897968: Chen R et al., PLoS One 2015;10(4):e0123703 - TZD vs placebo in T2DM, 27 RCTs. hsCRP SMD -0.65 (95%CI -0.98,-0.32); MCP-1 WMD -54.19 (-73.86,-34.52); vWF% -8.18; fibrinogen SMD -0.26; E-selectin -3.57 (pioglitazone-only). IL-6, MMP-9, sCD40L, PAI-1, ICAM-1 all NULL. PRIMARY SOURCE for the downgrade.
external_pmids.20926154: Zhao Y et al., Diabetes Res Clin Pract 2010;90(3):279-87 - 36 pioglitazone studies. Pioglitazone CRP SMD -0.577 (95%CI -0.732,-0.421) in 2-group studies; -0.327 in 1-group. Effect present in DM and non-DM.
external_pmids.16490432: Qayyum R & Adomaityte J, Am J Cardiol 2006;97(5):655-8 - TZD vs placebo, CRP -0.82 mg/L (95%CI -1.15,-0.49); diabetic subgroup -1.24 mg/L (p=0.008).

pioglitazone -> inflammation.what_is_validated: CRP/hsCRP lowering by pioglitazone in T2D - replicated across 3 independent meta-analyses spanning 2006-2015, consistent direction and magnitude, with a diabetes-specific subgroup effect.
pioglitazone -> inflammation.what_is_NOT_validated: IL-6 and TNF-alpha reduction (IL-6 pooled-null for pioglitazone; TNF-alpha never pooled). PAI-1/vWF/fibrinogen effects are rosiglitazone-specific. 'Independent of glucose lowering' rests on PIONEER (JACC 2005, pioglitazone vs glimepiride at matched HbA1c) - single-trial, not pooled.

oxidative_stress -> beta_cell.corpus_note: Single corpus PMID — mechanism is canonical, not novel to this corpus.

Hyperglycemia-induced ROS drives β-cell dysfunction via mitochondrial damage + ER stress + apoptosis
Antioxidant clinical evidence MIXED: vitamins limited; bardoxolone, sulforaphane, curcumin show some benefit
oxidative_stress -> beta_cell.confidence: HIGH for mechanism; therapeutic translation still mixed.

oxidative_stress -> T1D.corpus_note: Single corpus PMID. Mechanism canonical; external evidence supports pathogenic role.
external_evidence: Serum reactive oxygen metabolites elevated in T1D youth
Longitudinal plasma profiling: oxidative-stress markers + antioxidant-enzyme spike precede islet-autoimmunity conversion
Macrophages/DCs invade islets, activate via ROS, ferry β-cell antigens to pancreatic LNs → T-cell autoimmunity
oxidative_stress -> T1D.confidence: HIGH for pathogenesis; therapy-side translation still preclinical/early.

verapamil -> beta_cell.evidence: 2018 RCT (Ovalle et al, Nat Med) + 2023 meta-analysis (PMC10424102): verapamil improved stimulated C-peptide AUC at 3 and 12 months vs placebo in recent-onset T1D via TXNIP suppression and reduced beta-cell apoptosis. Mechanism + clinical outcome confirmed.

oxidative_stress -> inflammation.evidence: Frontiers Physiol 2018 + reviews: hyperglycemia/AGE-driven ROS triggers NF-kB priming of NLRP3, pro-IL-1beta/pro-IL-18 transcription, and inflammasome activation -> diabetic vascular/renal complications. Confirms oxidative-stress->inflammation linkage.

HCQ approved in India (DCGI, 400 mg/day) as T2D adjunct. Caveat: ~54% of RCTs poor Jadad quality, high performance/detection bias.

Mechanism via AMPK, reduced renal inflammation/oxidative stress. Note: observational, not RCT-grade for renal endpoints; SGLT2i/GLP-1 are guideline add-ons for DKD.

Dec 2025 Cureus mTOR review (cureus 439007) confirms bidirectional cytokine effects: mTORC1 inhibition lowers NF-kB/NLRP3 -> IL-1b/IL-18, reduces IL-17/IL-4, raises Tregs (anti-inflammatory side), BUT microglial IL-6 enhancement (PMC6806201) and dose-dependent immunostimulation persist. Net immunosuppressant, not pure anti-inflammatory. No rating change (MEDIUM, mixed).
rapamycin -> inflammation.revisit_note_3: REAFFIRMED PARTIALLY_VALIDATED (MIXED) on 2026-08-01. Fresh external check reconfirms bidirectional/context-dependent cytokine effects: 2026 PLOS One long-term rapamycin in aging (pone.0343183) shows reduced pro-inflammatory IL-12p40/IL-27/IL-17A AND concurrently reduced anti-inflammatory IL-10 upon LPS; classic mTOR paradox (Nature Rev Immunol nri2457: mTORC1 inhibition raises IL-12/IL-23/IL-6, lowers IL-10). Net immunosuppressant, not pure anti-inflammatory. No rating change (MEDIUM, mixed).

oxidative_stress -> T2D.evidence: Banik 2021 SR/MA (Health Sci Rep, PMID 34622023): 22 case-control studies, 2853 subjects; MDA & nitric oxide elevated, glutathione/total antioxidant status reduced in T2D vs controls. Pathogenic association well-supported. CAVEAT: antioxidant-supplementation RCTs have failed to show glycemic/prevention benefit, so association is robust but therapeutic causality unproven. | 2026-06-30 reaffirmed with fresh therapeutic-side evidence: resveratrol meta-analysis (Front Endocrinol 2024, DOI 10.3389/fendo.2024.1463027, PMC11771208; 6 RCTs, n=533) shows resveratrol significantly lowered CRP, lipid peroxides and 8-isoprostanes and raised GPx/catalase in T2D, BUT malondialdehyde, SOD, total antioxidant capacity, IL-6 and TNF-alpha were NOT significantly changed. NET: pathogenic oxidative-stress association remains robust; antioxidant-therapy signal is partial/marker-selective and therapeutic causality still unproven. Rating unchanged: VALIDATED (association), therapy=PARTIAL. | 2026-07-25 therapy-arm re-validation: THREE new 2025-26 RCT meta-analyses located. (1) Brandimonte-Hernandez/Gil, Nutrition Reviews 2026, DOI 10.1093/nutrit/nuaf292 (advance access; PMID pending) - 109 human RCTs of food bioactive compounds: alpha-lipoic acid and vitamin D produced SIGNIFICANT HbA1c reductions; zinc/selenium/chromium improved glycemic control + raised total antioxidant capacity/enzyme activity. (2) Vitamin C/E subgroup MA, Nutrition Reviews 2026, DOI 10.1093/nutrit/nuaf133 (PMC12793614): high-antioxidant-capacity C/E inversely associated with insulin resistance but agent/dose/duration dependent. (3) Astaxanthin MA 2026, DOI 10.1177/11786388261432862, 9 RCTs n=403 prediabetes/T2D: glycemic+lipid signal. NET: pathogenic association remains ROBUST (VALIDATED). Therapy-side signal is STRENGTHENED but remains AGENT-SPECIFIC (ALA, vit-D, Zn/Se/Cr show HbA1c benefit) and heterogeneous; classic antioxidant vitamins (C/E alone) stay weak. Therapy rating = PARTIALLY_VALIDATED (upgraded from marker-selective PARTIAL: now at least two agents show a hard glycemic endpoint, HbA1c). Therapeutic causality for 'antioxidants broadly' still unproven.

empagliflozin -> T2D.evidence: Multiple phase III RCTs: add-on to metformin HbA1c -0.70/-0.77% vs -0.13% placebo (PMID 24722494); add-on to pioglitazone +/- metformin -0.6/-0.7% (PMID 23906415); 78-wk add-on to basal insulin improved control (PMID 26040302). Glycemic efficacy firmly established.

oxidative_stress -> nephropathy.evidence: Consensus reviews (Diabetes/ADA Vol57; PMID 26906673 Diabetes & Kidney Disease: Role of Oxidative Stress; PMID 21557044): excess ROS via polyol/PKC/AGE-RAGE/hexosamine pathways + NADPH oxidases central to DKD initiation/progression (inflammation, ECM accumulation, fibrosis, glomerulosclerosis). Strong mechanistic support.

tacrolimus -> inflammation.evidence: REAFFIRMED PARTIALLY_VALIDATED (re-checked 2026-06-23). Bidirectional/context-dependent. Anti-inflammatory in T cells: tacrolimus inhibits NF-kB activation in peripheral human T cells (PLOS One, PMID 23573283), suppressing IL-2/TNFa/IL-6. Pro-inflammatory in vasculature: CNIs (tacrolimus, cyclosporine A) induce vascular inflammation & endothelial activation via TLR4 signaling -> increased ROS and NF-kB-regulated proinflammatory factors in endothelial/VSMCs; effect abolished in TLR4-/- aortas (Sci Rep srep27915, PMID 27295076 - corrected from prior 27291296). Net effect on inflammation NOT uniformly anti-inflammatory.
tacrolimus -> inflammation.note: No promotion - inherently context-dependent. PMID corrected: vascular-inflammation paper is 27295076 (was 27291296 in earlier note).
tacrolimus -> inflammation.revisit_2026_07_03: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED (context-dependent). Fresh 2025 source added: Pharmacological Reports 2025 review "Tacrolimus and diabetic rodent models" (PMID 39836342) - 48 studies; tacrolimus impairs islet beta-cell function via CaN/NFAT, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, TGF-beta/Smad and catalogs anti-inflammatory/antioxidant agents used to counter tacrolimus-induced diabetes, reinforcing pro-inflammatory/diabetogenic side. Vascular TLR4 pro-inflammatory paper (PMID 27295076) reaffirmed, no 2025-26 contradiction. Net effect NOT uniformly anti-inflammatory -> no promotion.
tacrolimus -> inflammation.revisit_2026_08_06: Reaffirmed PARTIALLY_VALIDATED (context-dependent, no promotion). Anti-inflammatory arm strengthened: 2025 narrative review 'Clinical applications of tacrolimus in ocular diseases' (PMID 41264132, Int Ophthalmol 2025) reiterates FKBP-12/calcineurin/NFAT inhibition suppressing IL-2 and pro-inflammatory cytokines and modulating Th17/Treg balance. Pro-inflammatory arm gained an independent second source: PMID 23958496 (CNIs recruit JAK2/JNK, TLR signaling and UPR to activate NF-kB-mediated inflammation in kidney tubular cells), complementing the vascular TLR4 finding (PMID 27295076). No 2025-26 contradiction of the bidirectional picture. Net effect NOT uniformly anti-inflammatory -> remains PARTIALLY_VALIDATED.

hydroxychloroquine -> inflammation.evidence: RCT/clinical (PMID 36777472, Int J Diabetes Dev Ctries 2023): 12-wk HCQ add-on in uncontrolled T2D significantly lowered IL-6 & hsCRP, raised adiponectin, with parallel improvement in beta-cell function & insulin resistance and HbA1c/FPG/PPG. Anti-inflammatory-mediated glycemic benefit supported.

GAD65 -> T1D.notes: DECISIVE NEGATIVE. The largest, HLA-enriched, confirmatory phase 3 of the hub-tracked antigen-specific tolerance strategy failed. Sponsor-offered contributing hypotheses (intralymphatic administration burden at low-volume sites; longer diagnosis-to-treatment interval; lower drug-product potency than DIAGNODE-2) are EXPLICITLY hypothesis-generating per the sponsor and must NOT be reported as established explanations. Subgroup numerical trends were underpowered and exploratory. SCOPE LIMIT: this contradicts MONOTHERAPY in recent-onset T1D. It does NOT directly test (a) LADA, where no pivotal data exist, (b) combination regimens (GAD-alum + vitamin D + etanercept), or (c) Stage 1/2 prevention. Downstream: GAD65-targeted CAR-Treg work is a different modality and is unaffected. NO peer-reviewed publication of DIAGNODE-3 exists yet - watch item.

colchicine -> inflammation.notes: Anti-inflammatory mechanism in diabetes is well supported and colchicine is cheap and generic - relevant to the repurposing arm. HONEST LIMITS: the CRP effect size is small; the IL-1beta adjustment analysis argues the vascular benefit may not be fully IL-1beta-mediated, so do NOT present NLRP3->IL-1beta as the demonstrated causal chain for the vascular endpoint. COLCOT-derived T2D evidence is post-MI secondary prevention, not primary diabetes therapy. No trial shows colchicine preserves beta-cell function.

alpha_lipoic_acid -> diabetic_neuropathy.notes: SPLIT BY ROUTE - this is the whole finding. IV 600 mg/day x 3 weeks produces a significant and clinically relevant reduction in neuropathic pain. ORAL >600 mg/day for 3-5 weeks shows statistically significant change whose CLINICAL relevance is unclear. Rated PARTIALLY_VALIDATED, not VALIDATED, because (a) the pivotal MAs are 2012-vintage, (b) the practical route for chronic outpatient care is oral - the weaker arm, (c) endpoints are symptom scores and nerve-conduction velocity, i.e. surrogate/subjective, with no hard outcome such as ulceration or amputation. Safety profile favourable (mainly stomach upset).

doctrine_notes.extraction_artifact_comparator_arms_2026: SYSTEMATIC EXTRACTION FLAW (found 2026-08-15). Drug names appearing in the trial-characteristics tables of systematic reviews / meta-analyses - i.e. as COMPARATOR or BACKGROUND therapy - are extracted as if they were the SUBJECT of a mechanistic claim, creating false 'drug -> outcome' paths. Single source PMID 35466661 (HCQ SR/MA) alone generated 5 such paths: atorvastatin->T2D, metformin->inflammation, pioglitazone->inflammation, pioglitazone->T2D, hydroxychloroquine->inflammation. The 2026-05-14 filter in build_research_paths.py caught only 3 because it required data_point_count==1; paths with repeated dose fragments (including an exact DUPLICATE fragment inflating dpc from 1 to 3) escaped. FIXED 2026-08-15: is_dose_fragment_artifact() now fires whenever EVERY key_claim is a non-mechanistic dose fragment, at any dpc. LESSON: data_point_count is NOT a proxy for evidential weight when the points can be duplicates from one table. Audit any path whose corpus_pmids is a single SR/MA.

The 13 corpus PMIDs above the legacy 42M 'fabrication' tripwire are all REAL 2026 records - reconfirming for the 5th time that the numeric cutoff is stale. Bulk esummary (100 IDs/request) is far cheaper than per-paper web search; make it the default vetting method.

2026-08-16_open_detector_loop.title: A working detector whose output nobody read
2026-08-16_open_detector_loop.finding: validate_citations.py had been correctly scoring miscited PMIDs as MISMATCH and writing them to citation_validation.json - for months. Nothing consumed that field. The daily credibility sweep only grepped for PMIDs >= 42,000,000 and for forbidden phrases, so it reported CLEAN on every run while 7 genuine miscitations sat in the build scripts, two of which resolved to PLANT BIOLOGY papers being cited as the DIAGNODE-2 trial and a GAD-alum meta-analysis.
2026-08-16_open_detector_loop.root_cause: Detection was decoupled from enforcement. The sweep tested for FABRICATED identifiers (out-of-range PMIDs) but never for MISATTRIBUTED ones - a real PMID pointing at the wrong paper passes every range check.
2026-08-16_open_detector_loop.secondary_finding: This also explains a long-standing open question: several off-topic oncology/infectious-disease papers sat in the corpus FLAGGED as "unclear relevance to diabetes research". They were ingested BECAUSE they were miscited. The flagged papers were the symptom; the miscitations were the cause.
2026-08-16_open_detector_loop.fix: Added Analysis/Scripts/check_citation_mismatches.py - a gate that reads citation_validation.json and exits non-zero on any unwhitelisted MISMATCH. Registered in run_quality_improvements.py immediately after validate. Suppression requires a written reason in WHITELIST (currently one entry: a regex example, not a citation).
2026-08-16_open_detector_loop.generalisation: Any detector this hub runs must have a consumer that can FAIL. An unread report is not a control.
2026-08-16_open_detector_loop.ordering_lesson: The claim inventory is cached in pmid_verification.json / paper_library/index.json. Editing a build script is NOT enough - verify_pmids.py -> ingest_papers.py -> build_paper_library.py -> validate_citations.py must be re-run in that order or the validator re-reports already-fixed mismatches.

2026-08-16_queue_blind_spot.title: Queue re-validated the validated and ignored the never-validated
2026-08-16_queue_blind_spot.finding: 14 of 57 research paths had NEVER been validated, while the work queue kept cycling re-validation of paths already rated VALIDATED. The "pick the stalest path" heuristic only ranks paths that already have a validation date, so a path with no date at all is invisible to it forever.
2026-08-16_queue_blind_spot.fix: Never-validated paths given priority 2 in the queue this run, ahead of re-validation of already-rated paths.
2026-08-16_queue_blind_spot.note: A prior alias-collision worry was checked and is NOT a real problem: only dorzagliatin->T2D is double-keyed.

2026-08-16_stale_publish_target.title: Green pipeline, frozen public site
2026-08-16_stale_publish_target.finding: docs/Dashboards/ - the copy GitHub Pages serves - had not changed since 2026-03-29/2026-04-20. 33 published dashboards stale, 2 missing, ZERO in sync, while run_quality_improvements.py reported "All 42 improvements completed successfully" on every daily run for roughly four months.
2026-08-16_stale_publish_target.root_cause: rebuild_website.py only ever wrote docs/index.html. No step copied rebuilt dashboards into docs/. The runner measured builder exit codes, not whether the published artifact changed.
2026-08-16_stale_publish_target.impact: The seven PMID miscitations corrected this run were still live publicly until this was fixed, as was a DIAGNODE-3 description superseded by the trial being closed for futility.
2026-08-16_stale_publish_target.fix: Added Analysis/Scripts/sync_docs_dashboards.py (copy + byte-equality re-verify, non-zero exit on failure), registered LAST in run_quality_improvements.py - after postprocess_dashboards.py, which rewrites Dashboards/*.html. Supports --check for drift-only reporting. 35/35 now in sync.
2026-08-16_stale_publish_target.generalisation: Same failure class as the citation MISMATCH gap found the same day: a step reporting success while the artifact a reader actually sees goes untouched. Verify the OUTPUT changed, not that the PRODUCER exited zero.

doctrine_notes.2026-08-17_state_integrity: THREE parallel path stores exist and had drifted: state["paths"] (57), state["validated_paths"] (59), and Analysis/Results/validated_research_paths.json (reports paths_validated=27). 16 paths were in state["paths"] but absent from state["validated_paths"]; 18 the reverse. The work-queue generator reads only ONE store, which is why the 2026-08-16 run emitted six "NEVER-VALIDATED" items for paths that had documented validations (SGLT2i_NLRP3_DKD 2026-04-24, teplizumab->autoimmune 2026-05-12, GLP1_RA->T1D 2026-06-21, etc). Stores reconciled this run. The dashboard figure "27 validated" understates the true count and should be regenerated from the reconciled store, not hardcoded.
doctrine_notes.2026-08-17_git_rootcause: GIT BLOCKER ROOT-CAUSED AND PARTLY FIXED - prior diagnosis was WRONG. It was recorded for 3 weeks as "a stale index.lock needing one manual delete". It is not. The OneDrive mount denies unlink() on files inside .git at ANY age (tested at 0s/20s/60s: all BLOCKED), so git cannot complete its write-index-lock-then-rename sequence and leaves a fresh lock behind on EVERY invocation. Deleting the lock on the host would have fixed exactly one run - which is why ~150 renamed lock corpses have accumulated in .git/ since April. WORKAROUND THAT WORKS: set GIT_INDEX_FILE to a path outside the mount (e.g. /tmp/gitidx) - git then writes its index off-mount, and objects/refs (create-new and rename-over, both permitted) succeed. Verified this run: 92 files staged, commit 3a737ed created, ending an 80-commit 3-week backlog. REMAINING BLOCKER IS DIFFERENT AND SMALLER: push fails with "could not read Username for https://github.com" - credentials only, no token in the sandbox. Commit is now automatable; push still needs the user. UPDATE (end of run): `git commit` succeeds only INTERMITTENTLY even with GIT_INDEX_FILE, because commit still touches .git/index.lock. The DETERMINISTIC recipe is plumbing + direct ref write, now codified in Analysis/Scripts/git_commit_safe.py: (1) GIT_INDEX_FILE off-mount, (2) git add -A, (3) git write-tree, (4) git commit-tree, (5) write .git/refs/heads/main by writing a temp file and os.rename() over it - NOT `git update-ref`, which needs HEAD.lock and fails. GOTCHA: write-tree/commit-tree print "unable to unlink tmp_obj_*" warnings onto stdout, so the SHA must be regex-extracted, not read via .strip(). ALL FUTURE RUNS SHOULD CALL git_commit_safe.py INSTEAD OF `git commit`. Confirmed working: commit 9437b70.
